announcements.title: Terminal sizing now respects your tmux config
announcements.body: Until now, resizing the portal terminal silently forced the whole tmux window to the browser's size — pinning it into manual mode and breaking your window-size setting (largest/smallest/latest) for every connected terminal. Fixed: the portal now behaves like any other tmux client, your policy decides, and previously stuck windows heal automatically when you open them in the portal. If you liked 'the browser always wins', set window-size latest in ~/.tmux.conf. Tip: window-size smallest keeps sessions fully visible even on a phone or tablet.
highlights: Your window-size policy works again — for every client
Stuck windows self-heal on portal attach (agentwire resize works too)
On a tablet? Try: set -g window-size smallest

announcements.title: You're an early one
announcements.body: AgentWire is young and shaped by the handful of people running it. Bug, idea, or just hello — open an issue, it's read.

announcements.title: New idea? Cmd+K and go.
announcements.body: AgentWire can now spin up a whole project from a single sentence. Press Cmd/Ctrl+K (or the New idea button), type — or speak — what you want to build, and it scaffolds the folder, starts an agent, and hands it your idea as the first message. You watch it get to work the moment the window opens.
highlights: Idea-first capture — type an idea, get a running agent
Instant voice mode — browser speech in and out, zero setup
